lines: Every night of the war, men crawled out between the trenches. Not to fight. To fix the wire.
They were called wiring parties. Coils of barbed wire, and iron posts that screw into the mud without a sound.
When a flare went up, they dropped flat and lay still until the dark came back.
Now the guns on Verdel Ridge have torn the Hegemony wire to pieces.
Wire stops a raid before it reaches the trench, and it catches the bullets that cross the line. Without it, every man on the fire step is easier to hit.
Tonight both sides can send a wiring party. Your soldier mends the wire in their own sector.
But a man out on the wire is a man not on watch. The side that stays home keeps its rifles on the parapet, and the other side's wiring party feels every one of them.
Comment WIRE under this post. Your soldier crawls out after dark. Results in the morning Gazette.
Mud and Iron. Every follower is a soldier.
